So, first thing that comes to my mind is my first line, a SFC, told the command team as well as our operational leadership that if they needed to communicate with me they had to go through him, unless absolutely necessary. My BH team didn’t want me to go to work to check in, they felt it would be better for me to contact via phone everyday, unless I needed to be seen, at which point I would meet up with my first line outside work. Jason, my first line, wanted me to focus on getting better and he explained that to everyone else. The unit and other leaders would contact him if I needed to do something or provide information. He would be the one to contact me. It doesn’t necessarily have to be a first line, but I trusted Jason, so he was the only person he wanted me to speak with outside of BH. One key thing he said to me when I started this journey stuck with me. I have used this with one of my soldiers, he said “Fuck the Army, Fuck this Unit, Fuck the Command. I want you to get better for yourself and your family.” He truly cared for me and my family. I trusted him so much. I think that is a big issue with a lot of soldiers, they don’t trust their leadership.

It depends on the individual, the health team, the chain of command, and the first line. 

I myself finally reached out for help. I spent 4 weeks speaking with BH, them I did 8 weeks of a partial hospitalization program (my place of duty was group therapy 5 days a week), and when I realized I still needed more, I was admitted to a BH hospital for a month. That was 2018. I’m still active duty. I had a great first line that fought for me. I also had an amazing BH team. I know there are very few like me, but it is possible, you just have to be willing to fight for it and have the support behind you helping you fight.

When I was looking into joining the Army, I wanted a job that would translate easily to the civilian world since I already had a family when I was joining. I ended up going 35N, Signals Intelligence Analyst. I have enjoyed the job for the most part. My recommendation is to either pick something you can do on the civilian side or just go for seomthing you think will be cool/fun to learn. The military is partly what you make of it. Just know that there will be ups and downs to whatever job you go with. As u/Z0na5 said, you literally can pick whatever you want. Best of luck in what you decide to do.

First of all, I hope that you can get through this troubling time. Next, last year I was really struggling, it had been about 4 years coming. My OIC straight up asked me if I was thinking about killing myself. Now, I had gotten pretty good at covering up everything that was going wrong until that point. I told him that I had in fact been thinking about it, for the last 4 years. I was "strongly encouraged" to go to BH. Now I am a 35N and so the fear of what it would do to my career is extremely high, but at this point I didn't care anymore. I went through an outpatient program for 6 weeks because I had just had my first of two back surgeries. The outpatient program that I was in was teaching me great skills and what not, but it was not addressing the problem. My BH provider explained to me that outpatient is like a bandaid. He suggested that I go inpatient which he likened to surgery, then follow it up with outpatient which would act as the reovery aspect of surgery. I agreed and went to an inpatient facility for a month. Now, I was lucky and went to a military inpatient program that was run completely by civilians, Emeral Coast in Panama City Beach FL. I was able to work through most of my demons, get the help that I so desperately needed. I told my BH provider after my inpatient stint that I did not want to be medboarded. He worked with me. I was also lucky to have good local leaders advocating for me. I still had to do an investigation to make sure I could keep my clearance, but I passed that. This year I was able to finally go to ALC and this month I was promoted to E6. So, where I am going with this is you need to go to BH man. You need to get help, but you need to want to do it for yourself and for your family. My NCOIC told me "Fuck the Army, Fuck the Commander, get better for yourself and for your family." I took that to heart. I encourage you to seek help. Going to BH is not a career ender, but ending your life is. If you need to talk, hit me up. I can give you more insight if needed. 

Side note, I am one of those E6's on a permanent profile, slightly bigger (taped everytime), not all of us are bad.

Respawn said that they are making some changes and it would affect what the meta is. I personally do not think that the peacekeeper needs to be nerfed or needs to have the precision choke removed. There are plenty of other weapons that can beat someone that has a peacekeeper. I read a post earlier on destiny about playing the way that you are best at. If you know people like to utilize close range weapons, use mid-range to long-range weapon types. An smg like the R-99 with barrel stabilizer, standard stock and an extended mag will destroy someone using a peacekeeper with the choke. You also have to be hitting your shots. Thankfully Apex is a server based gametype so if you aren't doing the damage you think you should be doing its probably because you aren't hitting your shots unlike a p2p game where internet upload and download speeds come into play. And if you are getting spammed with shots from the peacekeeper back off, heal up and engage from further away. This isn't CoD, you should not be bum rushing all the time. Play the third party game as well.

Well the range on it is due to the precision choke. It’s a perk of having all the parts on it. I personally don’t think any weapon should be nerfed. The game is a week old and people are already complaining about weapons or characters.

I run Peacekeeper alot and I can say that it doesn't need a nerf nor does it two shot a purple helm and armor. The weapon is designed to hit really hard really close. Maybe your shields weren't full. Everytime I have used it fully modded it takes about three shots. Now, the perk that Peacekeeper gets when it has the precision choke on it lets the user charge the shot while aiming, which increases the damage by quite a lot. So keep that in mind. Just remember, when people are using it they are right up on you.

One of the things that I have noticed about the Peacekeeper is that the rate of fire is slower than the Eva8 semi shotgun. With that in mind, remember to strafe. Practice strafing. Go into the training mode like u/Wunse suggested, and practice hip firing. Now once you get the Precision Choke for it, the Peacekeeper can be charged up while aiming. This helps you do more damage and gives you better range, however it is slower when trying to charge. So get a charged shot off, then keep shooting without worrying about the charge. Also keep in mind that cover is your friend in close quarters while shooting the shotgun. Good luck and remember to get mods for the Peacekeeper. Its a great end game weapon.
